articles.title: Drunk EV Driver Goes on Rampage in Surat? Four Injured as Speeding Car Smashes Multiple Vehicles
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Four people, including two brothers, were injured after an allegedly drunk driver lost control of his electric vehicle and rammed into multiple vehicles near Kanaiya Namkeen at Sarthana Jakat Naka in Surat on Tuesday night.

body.html:
Four people, including two brothers, were injured after an allegedly drunk driver lost control of his electric vehicle and rammed into multiple vehicles near Kanaiya Namkeen at Sarthana Jakat Naka in Surat on Tuesday night.

The accused has been identified as Vijay Shambhubhai Bhikhadia (32), an architect originally from Kundli village in Bhavnagar district's Talaja taluka. He currently resides in Purushottam Nagar Society near Shyamdham Temple in the Sarthana area of Surat.

According to police and local sources, the incident occurred on June 3 when Bhikhadia was driving his EV near Sarthana Jakat Naka. He allegedly lost control of the vehicle while under the influence of alcohol.

The car first hit a motorcycle carrying brothers Rohit Sarkhwada (24) and Ajay Sarkhwada (20), residents of Sargam Society in Punagam. The speeding vehicle then crashed into a scooter ridden by Rekhaben Pragjibhai Lakhani (53) and Hinaben Savani (37), both residents of the Sarthana Jakat Naka area.

The vehicle subsequently rammed into a car parked on the roadside, causing extensive damage to the motorcycle and the parked vehicle.

Local residents rushed to the scene and shifted the injured victims to a nearby private hospital for treatment. According to local sources, all four victims sustained serious injuries, including fractures and crush injuries to their limbs.

Eyewitnesses alleged that the driver appeared heavily intoxicated and was unable to stand properly after the accident. Angered by the incident, locals reportedly pulled him out of the vehicle and assaulted him. Some members of the crowd also damaged the EV by smashing its windows.

A team from Sarthana Police Station reached the spot after receiving information about the crash, rescued the accused from the mob and brought the situation under control.

During a search of the vehicle, police reportedly recovered an empty beer bottle. Bhikhadia was taken into custody and a case was registered against him for allegedly driving under the influence of alcohol and endangering public safety.

Police said further investigation is underway. CCTV footage of the incident has also surfaced and is being examined as part of the probe.

articles.title: Factory Lift Crashes Without Warning: Worker Killed on the Spot in Himmatnagar Industrial Tragedy
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A worker was killed in a tragic industrial accident after a heavy lift collapsed inside a factory in Gujarat's Sabarkantha district. The incident occurred on May 28 at Pramukh Industries in the GIDC area of Himmatnagar. The deceased has been identified as Devarajsinh Parmar.

body.html:
A worker was killed in a tragic industrial accident after a heavy lift collapsed inside a factory in Gujarat's Sabarkantha district. The incident occurred on May 28 at Pramukh Industries in the GIDC area of Himmatnagar.

The deceased has been identified as Devarajsinh Parmar. According to reports, routine operations were underway at the factory when the lift suddenly came crashing down.

Officials said Parmar was working near the lift and was directly beneath it when the structure collapsed. The heavy lift reportedly struck him on the head, causing fatal injuries. Witnesses said the lift fell suddenly and with such force that he had no chance to move to safety and became trapped underneath.

Co-workers rushed to the spot immediately after hearing the loud crash and attempted to rescue him. However, he succumbed to his injuries before any medical assistance could be provided.

The accident triggered panic among workers present at the factory. Employees described the incident as shocking, stating that the tragedy unfolded within seconds while normal operations were in progress.

The entire incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed inside the factory premises. The footage has since gone viral on social media, sparking outrage and raising concerns over workplace safety standards and industrial oversight.

The incident has also prompted questions about the maintenance, inspection and operation of heavy machinery within industrial facilities.

Police from Himmatnagar A-Division Police Station reached the scene and initiated an investigation. An accidental death case has been registered, and authorities are examining the circumstances that led to the lift collapse.

Investigators are looking into the possibility of mechanical failure, negligence or safety lapses. Further details are awaited.

The tragedy has once again brought attention to industrial safety concerns in Gujarat. About six months ago, two migrant workers were killed in a similar incident at an industrial unit in Surat district's Olpad taluka after a goods lift reportedly collapsed, resulting in fatal injuries.

articles.title: 3-Year-Old Child Among Two Killed in Horrific Pune Crash Caught on CCTV
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking CCTV video of a fatal road accident in Pune's Kharadi area has gone viral on social media, highlighting the dangers of reckless and wrong-side driving.

body.html:
A shocking CCTV video of a fatal road accident in Pune's Kharadi area has gone viral on social media, highlighting the dangers of reckless and wrong-side driving. The crash claimed the lives of a 35-year-old man and a three-year-old child after a speeding SUV allegedly rammed head-on into a motorcycle on the night of May 31.

According to police, the accident occurred around 10:30 pm in Samarth Nagar, Kharadi, when an SUV allegedly being driven at high speed on the wrong side of the road collided with a motorcycle carrying three people.

The deceased have been identified as Pawan Pandurang Bharambe (35) and Dipraj Tushar Kolhe (3). Pawan died at the scene, while Dipraj, who suffered critical injuries, later succumbed during treatment at a hospital.

A woman identified as Priya Tushar Kolhe (32), who was travelling on the motorcycle with the victims, sustained serious injuries and is currently undergoing treatment at a private hospital.

Police have arrested the SUV driver, Prasad More (25), a resident of Wagholi. He has been booked on charges of rash and negligent driving and causing death by negligence. Investigators have also found that he did not possess a valid driving licence.

According to Sub-Inspector Rahul Kolpe of Kharadi Police Station, officers suspect the accused may have attempted to destroy evidence after the accident. Police are also investigating whether he was under the influence of alcohol at the time of the crash.

The complaint in the case was lodged by Police Constable Amol Jadhav at Kharadi Police Station.

Prasad More was produced before a city court on Tuesday and has been remanded to police custody until June 5 for further investigation.

The entire incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed in the area. The footage, which has been widely circulated online, shows the alleged wrong-side collision and has sparked outrage among residents and road safety advocates.

Police have seized the CCTV footage and are examining all evidence as part of the ongoing investigation.

The tragedy has renewed concerns over increasing incidents of overspeeding, wrong-side driving and traffic rule violations in Pune, with many citizens demanding stricter enforcement and stronger road safety measures to prevent similar accidents in the future.

articles.title: Fuel Up and Flee: Thar Driver Caught on CCTV Escaping Without Paying for Diesel in Mathura
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A black Thar SUV carrying several young men allegedly fled a petrol pump in Uttar Pradesh's Mathura after getting its fuel tank filled with diesel without making any payment.

body.html:
A black Thar SUV carrying several young men allegedly fled a petrol pump in Uttar Pradesh's Mathura after getting its fuel tank filled with diesel without making any payment. The entire incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed at the fuel station, and the video has since gone viral on social media.

According to reports, the incident took place around 9:45 pm on Sunday at Dhangar Filling Station in the Jamunapar police station area. The Thar, which reportedly did not have a number plate, arrived at the petrol pump and asked an employee to fill the vehicle with diesel.

After the salesman filled the tank, he approached the vehicle to collect payment. However, as soon as the fuel cap was closed, the driver allegedly sped away from the petrol pump without paying.

The employee attempted to chase the vehicle, but the Thar quickly disappeared from the area within seconds.

The sudden incident left petrol pump staff shocked. The management immediately reviewed the CCTV footage, which clearly captured the sequence of events.

The petrol pump operator subsequently informed local police and lodged a complaint. Police have taken possession of the CCTV footage and launched an investigation into the matter.

Officials said they are also examining footage from CCTV cameras installed on nearby roads and intersections to identify the vehicle and the individuals involved.

Police stated that efforts are underway to trace the accused based on the available footage and that legal action will be taken once they are identified.

The incident has become a major talking point in the area, with the viral CCTV footage drawing widespread attention on social media.

articles.title: Newborn Stolen, Sold Across States? Ghaziabad Police Bust Child Trafficking Gang, Rescue
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Police in Ghaziabad's Tronica City area have busted an alleged interstate human trafficking network, arrested 12 accused and rescued an 11-day-old baby girl who was safely reunited with her family.

body.html:
Police in Ghaziabad's Tronica City area have busted an alleged interstate human trafficking network, arrested 12 accused and rescued an 11-day-old baby girl who was safely reunited with her family.

The operation was launched after a woman named Hina filed a complaint on May 26 alleging that her newborn daughter had been taken from her home by a woman identified as Puja. Based on the complaint, an FIR was registered at Tronica City Police Station under relevant sections related to kidnapping and common intention, and multiple teams were formed to trace the infant and arrest those involved.

According to DCP (Rural) Surendra Nath Tiwari, police used CCTV footage, surveillance, informers and manual intelligence gathering to track down the accused. During the operation, police arrested 12 people and recovered the baby girl. Three cars and counterfeit currency worth Rs 2.90 lakh were also seized.

The arrested accused have been identified as Sunil Kumar, Krishna Devi, Sanjay Kumar, Rajendra Singh, Pawan Kumar, Manoj Prakash alias Monu, Vineet Kumar, Rabiya, Jyoti, Puja, Farmina and Kumkum.

Police said the gang allegedly targeted vulnerable families and attempted to acquire newborn children by luring parents with money. Investigators revealed that efforts were initially made to convince the infant's mother to part with her child. However, after she refused, the baby was allegedly kidnapped from the family home.

During interrogation, Rabiya allegedly told police that Hina is her sister-in-law and that she had tried to persuade her to sell the child even before the birth. She allegedly contacted Monu and Puja, who were said to be operating the trafficking network, and an agreement was reportedly made to sell the infant for Rs 2 lakh.

However, after the baby girl was born on May 23, Hina reportedly changed her mind and refused to hand over the child. Police allege that after learning this, Monu pressured Rabiya to deliver the infant, claiming arrangements had already been made for the child's sale. Investigators say Rabiya subsequently kidnapped the newborn and handed her over to the trafficking network.

Police further alleged that the gang had arranged to sell the infant to a couple in Andhra Pradesh through other members of the network who remain absconding. Investigators suspect the group had previously sold several children to buyers in Andhra Pradesh and other locations.

Authorities said the accused were gathering at a secluded location near a temple in Tronica City to complete the transaction when police raided the spot and rescued the child.

According to ACP Siddharth Gautam, the gang also used counterfeit currency during child trafficking operations. The accused allegedly used fake notes to purchase children from vulnerable families. By the time victims discovered the money was counterfeit, the child would already have been taken away, making it difficult for them to approach authorities.

Police also stated that the gang used multiple vehicles interchangeably during trafficking operations to avoid detection and identification.

Additional sections related to theft, human trafficking and criminal conspiracy have been added to the case. Police said five accused identified as Raju, Deepti, Aarti, Tarannum and Nadeem are still absconding. Three special teams have been formed to trace and arrest them.

Further investigation is underway to determine the full extent of the trafficking network and identify any additional victims.

#Ghaziabad #HumanTrafficking #ChildTrafficking #BreakingNews

articles.title: ‘Talking to a Girl’ Led to Brutal Assault? Viral Aligarh Video Sparks Outrage, 3 Arrested
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A video allegedly showing a young man and a young woman being assaulted at the Aligarh Exhibition Ground has gone viral on social media, triggering outrage and prompting police action. The incident reportedly took place on the night of June 2, 2026, at the exhibition ground in Aligarh.

body.html:
A video allegedly showing a young man and a young woman being assaulted at the Aligarh Exhibition Ground has gone viral on social media, triggering outrage and prompting police action.

The incident reportedly took place on the night of June 2, 2026, at the exhibition ground in Aligarh. According to allegations, a young man was surrounded and assaulted after he was seen with a young woman. The attackers are believed to include the woman's relatives and their associates.

The viral video shows the young man being beaten with belts, punches and kicks. When the young woman attempted to intervene and protect him, she was allegedly pushed and assaulted as well.

The incident, which occurred in a public place, has raised concerns over law and order and the growing tendency of individuals taking matters into their own hands instead of seeking legal remedies.

Following the circulation of the video, police launched an investigation to verify the authenticity of the footage, establish the exact location of the incident and identify those involved.

According to police, the complainant had visited the Mangal Bazaar exhibition with a friend on June 2 and was talking to an acquaintance when the accused allegedly abused and assaulted him with belts.

Based on the complaint, FIR No. 407/2026 was registered at Banna Devi Police Station under Sections 115(2), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

As part of the investigation, police arrested three accused identified as Akash, son of Rajendra; Ankur, son of Ramji Lal; and Ashish, son of Jaipal. All three are residents of the Banna Devi police station area in Aligarh.

The arrests were made by the Banna Devi Police Station team from within the police station jurisdiction.

The police team involved in the operation included Sub-Inspector Ravi Pawan Kumar and Constable Rohit Kumar.

Police said further legal action is being taken and the investigation remains ongoing.

articles.title: Hunter Becomes the Trapped: Leopard Stuck in Chicken Coop After Killing 10 Birds in Uttarakhand
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A leopard became trapped inside a chicken coop in Uttarakhand's Pauri district on Tuesday morning after entering the enclosure in search of prey. The animal remained stuck for nearly two hours and killed 10 chickens before being rescued by the forest department.

body.html:
A leopard became trapped inside a chicken coop in Uttarakhand's Pauri district on Tuesday morning after entering the enclosure in search of prey. The animal remained stuck for nearly two hours and killed 10 chickens before being rescued by the forest department.

The incident took place in the Mason Talla area, where around 50 chickens were grazing inside a poultry enclosure. At around 6 am, the leopard emerged from a nearby forest and entered the coop looking for food.

As the predator attacked the birds, panic broke out among the chickens. In the chaos, the leopard killed 10 chickens. However, while chasing its prey, it moved deeper into the enclosure and became trapped, unable to find a way out.

The loud cries of the chickens alerted nearby residents, who rushed to the spot and were shocked to find a leopard trapped inside the coop. A large crowd soon gathered outside as the animal repeatedly attempted to escape. The unusual scene attracted widespread attention in the area, with panic and curiosity prevailing among villagers.

Upon receiving information, a forest department team rushed to the location and first cleared the crowd to ensure safety. Wildlife experts then formulated a plan to safely rescue the animal.

After an operation lasting around an hour, the leopard was tranquilised and safely captured. Officials said special care was taken to ensure that neither the animal nor any residents were harmed during the rescue.

According to forest department officials, the leopard was successfully secured after being tranquilised, and further necessary action was taken. Villagers later praised the forest department team for carrying out the rescue operation safely.

The incident has once again highlighted the growing human-wildlife conflict in several parts of Garhwal, including Pauri district. Forest officials and wildlife experts noted that leopards are increasingly entering villages in search of food due to the shrinking gap between forested areas and human settlements.

Experts believe poultry farms, domestic animals and improperly disposed organic waste often attract wild animals towards populated areas. Authorities have advised residents to immediately inform the forest department in such situations rather than gathering crowds near trapped or distressed wildlife.

articles.title: Death Beneath a Giant Hoarding: 24-Year-Old Crushed as Illegal Structure Collapses During Storm
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 24-year-old victim, identified as Amit Mohan Sukale was killed after a large unauthorised hoarding collapsed onto a road in Rasin village of Maharashtra's Karjat taluka during heavy rain and strong winds on Sunday night.

body.html:
A 24-year-old victim, identified as Amit Mohan Sukale was killed after a large unauthorised hoarding collapsed onto a road in Rasin village of Maharashtra's Karjat taluka during heavy rain and strong winds on Sunday night.

According to local officials, the incident occurred amid stormy weather that lashed the region, causing the massive hoarding to give way and crash onto the roadway.

A banner for an event had been placed on the hoarding. Fearing that the intense wind would tear the expensive flex banner, the youth was asked to climb the structure to pierce holes in the material, which would allow the wind to pass through and reduce the pressure.

Residents alleged that the hoarding had been erected without proper authorisation, raising serious concerns over safety violations and regulatory oversight.

The incident has triggered demands for strict action against those responsible for installing the structure.

Police and local authorities rushed to the spot soon after the collapse and cleared the debris from the road.

An investigation has been launched to determine the exact cause of the incident and to verify whether the hoarding had the required permissions.

Officials said appropriate action will be taken based on the findings of the inquiry.

The tragedy has once again highlighted concerns over the presence of unauthorised hoardings in public spaces, especially during the monsoon season when strong winds and heavy rainfall significantly increase the risk of structural failures.

articles.title: Trekker Missing for 6 Days in Uttarkashi: Friends Questioned as Search Shifts to Lake Near Campsite
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 23-year-old trekker, Babita Pandey, has been missing since May 29 during a trekking trip in Uttarakhand's Uttarkashi district. Police have taken the two friends who were last seen with her in CCTV footage in for questioning as part of the ongoing investigation.

body.html:
A 23-year-old trekker, Babita Pandey, has been missing since May 29 during a trekking trip in Uttarakhand's Uttarkashi district. Police have taken the two friends who were last seen with her in CCTV footage in for questioning as part of the ongoing investigation.

According to police, the last CCTV footage of Babita Pandey was recorded in Raithal village, where she was seen along with the two men. They are currently being questioned at Maneri Police Station.

The two have been identified as Harman Pal Singh, a resident of Dineshpur in Uttarakhand's Udham Singh Nagar district, and Harmanpreet Singh, a resident of Shahjahanpur in Uttar Pradesh. Both are 23 years old.

Police said the three left Udham Singh Nagar on May 25 for a trip to Uttarkashi. They stayed in Dehradun on the same day and reached Harsil on May 26.

The group reportedly spent May 26 and 27 visiting Harsil, Gangotri and other nearby tourist destinations before staying in Raithal village on May 28.

On May 29, the trio left for Dayara Bugyal and stayed at Goi Base Camp. According to police, Babita Pandey went missing from the campsite, triggering a large-scale search operation and investigation.

Six days after her disappearance, the search has entered a crucial phase, with authorities now focusing on a lake located near the campsite from where she was last reported missing.

Over the past several days, teams from the SDRF, NDRF, police, forest department and other agencies have conducted extensive searches across forests, trekking routes, slopes and other difficult terrain. However, no significant breakthrough has been made so far.

Officials believe the lake may provide an important lead in the case. A six-member special deep-search team is expected to reach the location and begin operations using modern equipment to thoroughly examine the lake and surrounding area.

Local residents and officials are closely monitoring the operation, hoping the intensified search effort will help uncover fresh clues in the disappearance of the missing trekker.

articles.title: 40-Foot Well Turns Death Trap for Deer, Villagers Risk Lives in Dramatic Rescue Operation
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Two deer that accidentally fell into a 40-foot-deep well in a field on the outskirts of Nandan village in Gujarat's Una taluka were rescued after a joint operation by the forest department and local villagers.

body.html:
Two deer that accidentally fell into a 40-foot-deep well in a field on the outskirts of Nandan village in Gujarat's Una taluka were rescued after a joint operation by the forest department and local villagers. Both animals were later shifted to an animal care centre for treatment and observation.

The incident occurred around noon at the farm of Ramjibhai Lakhmanbhai Mewada. The agricultural area is located close to a forest, where wild animals frequently venture towards human settlements in search of water or while roaming. During one such movement, the two deer reportedly fell into a water-filled well.

After spotting the animals trapped inside the well, local farmers immediately alerted the forest department. Upon receiving the information, Una Forest Department Forester Jitendrabhai Bambhaniya and his team rushed to the spot.

A rescue operation was launched with the help of local forest ranger Bharatbhai and several village youths. Using ropes, the volunteers descended into the 40-foot-deep well and carefully rescued both deer in an operation that lasted several hours.

Forest officials said the animals were visibly frightened and trembling after being pulled out. The department immediately provided first aid before shifting them to the nearest animal care centre for further treatment and care.

Speaking about the rescue, Vanamitra Bharatbhai said, "We cannot ignore the suffering of a voiceless animal. It was our moral duty to help. Since the forest and village boundaries are close, such incidents occur, but villagers and the forest department are always ready to protect wildlife."

Forester Jitendrabhai Bambhaniya praised the prompt response and courage shown by the villagers. He said such incidents are common in agricultural areas located along forest borders and stressed the need for fencing or covering open wells to prevent wildlife from falling into them in the future.

The successful rescue has once again highlighted the concern and compassion shown by the people of the Una region towards wildlife conservation.
